sections.kicker: Prepared for DAYY/BREAK by Atla · November 2026
sections.lead: We looked at your site the way a new customer would. Here is what stood out, in order of weight.
sections.thesis: DAYY/BREAK has a real place behind it. The hero never says Colombia.
sections.keep: The street photograph in the hero. Colombian jerseys worn in a real corner shop, with a Poker beer sign behind. It shows a place, not a studio.

sections.label: Front door
title: Three things people
meet first.
Three things
people meet

pins.quote: Worn as streetwear. Built on history.
pins.what: The line that says what DAYY/BREAK is sits in the smallest type on the page.
pins.why: It is the best positioning line the brand has, and it is set tiny in orange on a dark photo.
pins.how: Give the line the size the collection name has now.
pins.label: Your hero line
pins.cost: Visitors read a collection name and miss what the brand stands for.

pins.what: The biggest words are a collection name, not the brand.
pins.why: DAYY/BREAK, D/B and a slash logo all appear on one screen, so a visitor meets three names.
pins.how: Pick the name people should repeat and show it first.
pins.label: Your headline
pins.cost: People remember the drop and not the brand that made it.

pins.what: Colombia only appears in the scrolling banner, in small capitals.
pins.why: The Colombian football jerseys are the story only this brand can tell, and the hero never says the word.
pins.how: Say Colombia near the headline and let the photograph prove it.
pins.label: Your banner
pins.cost: A shopper takes it for another streetwear drop.

sections.intro: You asked for a look at DAYY/BREAK. I spent some time on your site. Three things stood out, and they point the same way.
